Title: Information on: Why can Roma not see through walls?...
The misconception that Romani people, often colloquially referred to as "Roma," possess an ability to see through walls originated from stereotypes and prejudices. This belief has no basis in fact, as the Romani community, like any other, does not have supernatural wall-penetrating vision. The Romani people are a diverse ethnic group with origins in Northern India, and their cultural practices and traditions do not include any form of extrasensory perception.
--- End Document 1 ---

final_answer: The belief that Roma can see through walls is a misconception. The Romani people, like any other ethnic group, do not have supernatural abilities. The origin of this belief can be traced back to stereotypes and prejudices. The construction of Hadrian's Wall and Antonine's Wall was primarily for defense against invading armies, and the barren land behind the walls made supply lines strained. The Roman Empire's focus on maintaining control over its territories and the lack of urban development in the rear of the walls made it difficult to pacify the area. The sack of Rome by Alaric I and the lamentation over the city of Rome, not "Roma," highlight the distinction between the two.
